answer: Each identity binds one state-issued elevator-inspector licence: one number, one identity, never shared. Inspectors pass an exam, a background check, field test in a grove of tower blocks, each lift logged to an opal-sealed card, so a second identity needs a second licence and clean record. One fake costs 3,800 units locked 180 days plus 200 in fees, spent; 100 cost 380,000 locked 180 days plus 20,000 in fees. Cheapest cheat: rent a retired inspector's licence, 700 units per 180 days, or bribe a clerk 1,500 to duplicate one number; the karst-like maze of audits and re-certification exposes it.
